scope: Amy M. Bertani-Tomczak and Sarah Jones, Will County, Illinois
purpose: Evidence ledger for 2026 retention profiles. These are trial-court actions described by reviewing courts, not appellate opinions authored by the retention judges.
methodology: Read the official Illinois Courts PDF texts, including procedural posture and disposition. Search snippets were leads only.
Separate trial action and stated reasoning from the reviewing court's analysis. A criminal sentence, conviction, affirmance, or reversal is not coded as a party vote.
This selected-case sample is not a complete docket audit or an estimated reversal rate. No personal ideology, current partisan affiliation, Trump support, or numeric Trump score is inferred.
Subsequent-history searches are limited public-web checks, not a citator or live docket certification. Unknown later proceedings remain explicit.

rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge, identified in caption; not an appellate panel member.
rulings.issue: Pretrial detention and whether release conditions could mitigate danger.
rulings.trialAction: Granted the State's petition to detain a defendant accused of armed vehicular hijacking and robbery.
rulings.trialReasoning: The reported explanation emphasized a handgun, bodily harm, an elderly victim, alleged car hijacking, and masks.
rulings.appellateDisposition: Affirmed 2–1. The majority found the evidence and circumstances sufficient under the detention statute and abuse-of-discretion review. Justice McDade dissented because the State had not supplied evidence that conditions could not mitigate danger.
rulings.appellateAuthors: Justice Albrecht; Justice Hettel concurred; Justice McDade dissented.

supportingExcerpt.text: handgun, bodily harm, senior citizen, an alleged hijacking of a car, masks

rulings.publicationStatus: Rule 23 order, not precedent except as allowed by Rule 23(e)(1). Official index metadata still labels it Slip as of November 1, 2026.
rulings.subsequentHistory: No later case-specific disposition independently established by this review.
rulings.possibleIssueComparison: Pretrial liberty versus detention for case-specific public-safety risks.
rulings.comparisonLimit: Applying Illinois' detention statute in one violent-crime case does not establish opposition to bail reform, a political party preference, or Trumpism.

rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge, identified in caption; not an appellate panel member.
rulings.issue: Access to an evidentiary hearing on a young adult's constitutional challenge to mandatory life imprisonment.
rulings.trialAction: Dismissed the amended postconviction petition at its second stage.
rulings.trialReasoning: The opinion reports only that she reviewed the petition and dismissal motion; it does not supply a fuller trial rationale. The original life sentence was mandatory.
rulings.appellateDisposition: Affirmed dismissal of the federal Eighth Amendment claim; reversed dismissal of the Illinois proportionate-penalties claim and remanded. The expert report and case-specific allegations warranted an evidentiary hearing. The court did not invalidate the sentence.
rulings.appellateAuthors: Justice Peterson; Justices Holdridge and Davenport concurred.

supportingExcerpt.text: Absent an evidentiary hearing, the dismissal of defendant’s petition was premature.

rulings.publicationStatus: Slip opinion, listed as Slip on the official index when checked. The opinion may change on rehearing.
rulings.subsequentHistory: A 2022 order had reversed first-stage dismissal and ordered second-stage proceedings. No later disposition of the October 2026 opinion or remand independently established.
rulings.possibleIssueComparison: Sentencing review, rehabilitation, and emerging-adult constitutional claims.
rulings.comparisonLimit: This is a procedural entitlement-to-hearing decision. Do not label the mandatory original sentence a discretionary ideological choice or call the defendant exonerated.

judges.name: Sarah Jones
judges.court: Circuit Court of the 12th Judicial Circuit, Will County

rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge, identified in caption; not an appellate panel member.
rulings.issue: Police stop, due process, and admissibility of custodial statements after part of an interrogation went unrecorded.
rulings.trialAction: Denied suppression and quashing of arrest, finding a lawful investigatory stop and voluntary, reliable statements. Found the recording failure unintentional.
rulings.trialReasoning: The reported findings considered the stop circumstances, the defendant's age and capacities, and his lack of objection when officers repeated his earlier statement after recording began.
rulings.appellateDisposition: Affirmed. The panel found reasonable suspicion, no due-process violation, and sufficient voluntariness/reliability under the statutory exception, considering Miranda waiver, food/restroom opportunities, and the overall interrogation.
rulings.appellateAuthors: Justice McDade; Justices Holdridge and O’Brien concurred.

supportingExcerpt.text: The trial court found that the failure to record was unintentional.

rulings.publicationStatus: Final, according to the official index metadata saved in will-index-sarah-jones.json; modified on denial of rehearing October 2, 2014.
rulings.subsequentHistory: No later case-specific disposition independently established by this review.
rulings.possibleIssueComparison: Police investigative authority and protections against unlawful seizure or involuntary statements.
rulings.comparisonLimit: A fact-specific suppression ruling is not a position on police immunity, federal policing policy, party affiliation, or Trump.
rulings.recordingCaveat: At paragraph 52 the appellate panel cautioned that mere silence may not establish agreement with police summaries; that issue was not before it because the defendant conceded accuracy on appeal.

rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge, identified in caption; not an appellate panel member.
rulings.issue: Scope of a criminal restriction on a registered offender's presence at facilities serving children.
rulings.trialAction: Denied a directed verdict and convicted Haberkorn after a bench trial for being on an Easter Seals field-trip bus; imposed probation.
rulings.trialReasoning: The opinion describes the evidence and outcome, but does not set out Jones's full statutory rationale.
rulings.appellateDisposition: Reversed conviction and sentence. The facility/program/bus also served adults; the State had not proved the statutory requirement that services be directed exclusively to children. Review was de novo, with the panel also finding evidence insufficient under a deferential standard.
rulings.appellateAuthors: Justice Schmidt; Presiding Justice Carter and Justice McDade concurred.

supportingExcerpt.text: Accordingly, we reverse defendant’s conviction and sentence.

rulings.publicationStatus: Final, according to the official index metadata saved in will-index-sarah-jones.json.
rulings.subsequentHistory: No later case-specific disposition independently established by this review.
rulings.possibleIssueComparison: Strict construction of criminal restrictions and proof of each statutory element.
rulings.comparisonLimit: The appellate policy criticism of broad offender-registration rules belongs to the appellate panel, not Jones. No party or Trump alignment is inferred from the conviction.
rulings.trialActionDateNote: July 2016 is the reported commencement of the bench trial; exact conviction date was not stated in the reviewed opinion.

rulings.judgeRole: Trial judge, called Sarah F. Jones in official caption; not a supreme court justice.
rulings.issue: Unresolved substitution motion and statutory limits on extended sentencing.
rulings.trialAction: Continued the substitution motion at counsel's request; never ruled on it. Later conducted the bench trial and imposed concurrent nine-year DUI and six-year revoked-license terms.
rulings.trialReasoning: No merits denial of substitution occurred. The opinion does not report Jones's reason for the extended term.
rulings.appellateDisposition: Reversed the appellate judgment overturning the convictions: the substitution motion was abandoned by failing to obtain a ruling. Affirmed the DUI sentence, vacated the unauthorized extended term on the lesser offense, and ordered a three-year term.
rulings.appellateAuthors: Justice Cunningham; Theis, Neville, Overstreet, Holder White and Rochford concurred; O’Brien did not participate.

supportingExcerpt.text: the judge never entered a ruling on the motion

rulings.publicationStatus: Final, according to the official index metadata saved in will-index-sarah-jones.json.
rulings.subsequentHistory: Actual implementation of the sentencing remand was not independently checked.
rulings.possibleIssueComparison: Access to an impartial tribunal and lawful sentencing limits.
rulings.comparisonLimit: Do not describe the substitution motion as denied or infer actual bias from the motion's allegation. This record does not support partisan alignment.
